hints.content:
The basic function $\cos(x)$ has a maximum point at $(0,1)$ and intersects its midline at $\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2},0\right)$.

$\qquad$![](${☣ LOCALPATH}/images/045d194412b500fdd873c28902f2f903.png)

Let's transform $\pink{\cos(x)}$ to $\blue{2\cos(0.5x-0.25\pi)-5}$ step by step and see how the graph changes along the way.

The transformation from $\pink{\cos(x)}$ to $\green{\cos(0.5x)}$ is a horizontal stretch by a factor of $\dfrac{1}{0.5}=2$, so the intersection point's horizontal distance from the origin is stretched from $\dfrac{\pi}{2}$ to $\pi$.

$\qquad$![](${☣ LOCALPATH}/images/1ce279987cf76d726a8d4081c5276b34.png)

The transformation from $\green{\cos(0.5x)}$ to $\red{2\cos(0.5x)}$ is a vertical stretch by a factor of $2$, so the maximum point's vertical distance from the origin is stretched from $1$ to $2$.

$\qquad$![](${☣ LOCALPATH}/images/11f050646ffcc486cd29cc7e62aae98f.png)

The transformation from $\red{2\cos(0.5x)}$ to $\blue{2\cos(0.5x-0.25\pi)-5}$, which is equivalent to $2\cos{\large(}0.5(x-0.5\pi){\large)}-5$, is a translation to the right by $0.5\pi$ units and a translation downwards by $5$ units.

As a result of these transformations, the maximum point is now at $\left(0.5\pi,-3\right)$ and the intersection with the midline is at $(1.5\pi,-5)$.

The resulting graph looks as follows:

$\qquad$![](${☣ LOCALPATH}/images/285f3196e0885a71a3bdb1818c1415fc.png)
